status_summary: No directive refocusing the Bureau of Justice Statistics or the National Institute of Justice was found. Public Law 119-74, approved 2026-01-23, funds the Office of Justice Programs research, evaluation and statistics account at 55 million dollars (33 million for statistics and 22 million for research and evaluation), which CRS reports is about 15.4 percent below fiscal year 2025 and equal to the administration's request. That funding direction runs opposite to the text's call to prioritize and sufficiently fund the National Crime Victimization Survey, although the survey's own funding line was not identified. The survey continues; the BJS survey page lists a March 2026 report as its latest.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-74 (Commerce, Justice, Science appropriations for fiscal year 2026) is approved, providing 55 million dollars for OJP research, evaluation and statistics, of which 33 million is for criminal justice statistics programs and 22 million for research, development and evaluation.

title: Refocus BJS and NIJ and prioritize funding for the National Crime Victimization Survey
uncertainties: No directive refocusing the Bureau of Justice Statistics or the National Institute of Justice was found. Public Law 119-74 (2026-01-23) funds the OJP research, evaluation and statistics account at 55 million dollars, about 15.4 percent below FY2025 per CRS, which runs against the text's funding element; the survey's own funding line was not identified, and the FY2025 split was not read in a primary source. Federal Register searches found only routine notices; H.R. 2240 does not qualify; the BJS site shows no refocus notice; one news search found no directive. The Justice list in the reginfo.gov Unified Agenda (Agency Rule List - 2026, 76 rules) holds no related entry. Separation of official from contractor reports was not checked. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
